title: Wajima chinkin bowl
summary: Turn a soup bowl on a high foot, coat it in black lac, then cut fine lines, vines and bamboo leaves into the surface and fill them with gold.
howToPlay: The bowl in its frame shows what to make.
Drag across the wood to set its width, then tap the bands to lay the lac.
Pick a graver and scrape each lit mark; gold leaf fills the groove.
rules: Shape counts for half the score, the lac on each band for a quarter, and the engraved marks for a quarter.
Three gravers cut three marks: a line, a vine and a bamboo leaf.
Three stars for 88 or more, two stars for 65 and one star for 40. Watch and learn makes a whole piece for you.
heritageNote: Chinkin is a Japanese lacquer technique: fine lines are cut into hardened lac with a chisel and gold leaf or powder is rubbed into the grooves, so the pattern glows against the dark ground.
